title: Woody Herman tears up his contract
summary: Tizol had signed with Woody Herman but Herman let him go to James; he made one Herman recording including Perdido.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Yesterday when we were talking, you were telling me about when Harry James called you to join his band, we didn't mention Woodie Herman, and in reading Stanley Dance's interview with you, I see that you had already made arrangements to go with Woodie Herman? Tell me about that.

Yes. I told Duke that I was going, when I was getting ready to quit, that I had signed with Woodie Herman to go with him, and later on when what's his name -- when Harry James called me, I had quit the band and Harry James had called me to go with him, I told Woodie Herman to see if he didn't mind to let me off, because after all, I wanted to go home, which I hadn't been in a whole year, almost. I could be there, and I wanted to see my wife, and I'd be back in Washington.
So he said, 'That's all right, Juan; if you want to go ahead, that's all right. I wish you a lot of luck'. And I left the band.
Yeah, he tore the contract up.
That was pretty unusual, wasn't it?
That was pretty darn nice of him.
Woodie is a pretty nice guy, huh?
I did one recording with him.
I know one of the two was Perdido, I know that.
Oh, gosh; I don't know. That's when I left Duke Ellington, you know?
Was that around the time that you were supposed to go with Woodie's band?
Was it recorded in New York?
